answer: Vertex-Split Referral Ledger. Each new agent identity must be invited by an existing one, and the inviter's ledger records its children. Standing is capped by a concave function of the ledger subtree: total influence grows with the square root of descendants, so clones added by one inviter dilute its share rather than multiply it. A knoll of capital buys many identities but near-zero marginal weight. The inviter also posts a cedar-denominated reserve per child that vests only on that child's genuine activity; cloned children forfeit the reserve, making each marginal clone a net loss.
